newsitem.title: USA: U.S. late spot LPGs leap with crude, bullish EIAs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. late spot LPGs leap with crude, bullish EIAs.

text.p: U.S. spot LPG prices jumped sharply across the board Wednesday sparked by a combination of rising crude oil prices and bullish new monthly EIA propane data.
Strength on crude oil markets, inspired by tensions in Iraq, helped boost LPG prices almost two cents a gallon in Mont Belvieu, to between 46.50 and 47.00 cents, players said.
"Inventories are an even bigger factor," one Texas trader said, noting EIA data released Wednesday showed Gulf Coast propane stocks 5.4 million barrels shy of this time last year.
Gulf stocks grew by 400,000 barrels for the month ending August 31, the EIA said.
Midwest propane stocks gained 2.3 million barrels and U.S. inventories grew a scant 2.1 million, the report said.
At Conway, Kansas, propane jumped to 44.50 cents a gallon.
Most butanes at both centers also firmed, traders said.
